top.title: Barcelona in line for potential €12m windfall as former winger emerges as a target for PSG
top.description: Barcelona in line for potential €12m windfall as former winger emerges as a target for PSG According to Le Parisien (h/t Mundo Deportivo ), PSG are considering a move for Real Betis winger Ez Abde as they prepare to strengthen their attack in January, and Barcelona could benefit financially from the operation. The 24-year-old former Blaugrana attacker is among the names being evaluated by PSG and a transfer could see the Catalans receive a potential €12 million windfall. PSG eyeing Abde The current French and European champions have been hurt by injuries in the attacking department as two regular starters, Khvicha Kvaratskhelia and Desire Doue, have both suffered from ruptured ACLs, ruling them out for a long period. Luis Enrique & co. still have the likes of Maghnes Akliouche and Mika Godts as alternatives, while two former Barcelona stars, Ferran Torres and Ousmane Dembele, are also optons even though they have played centrally in recent seasons. Nonetheless, PSG are looking at the market to reinforce their attacking unit and Abde, who has excelled at Real Betis since leaving Barcelona, has emerged as an option. PSG interested in Abde. (Photo by Octavio Passos/Getty Images) The Moroccan international is among several players that Les Parisiens are considering, including Antonio Nusa of RB Leipzig and Chelsea youngster Estevao, among others. Barcelona, though, will be watching the situation closely, as Abde’s transfer could bring them a sizeable revenue boost. Why Barcelona stand to gain That is because, the Blaugrana still retain a 20% stake in the winger’s economic rights when he joined Real Betis permanently. With Abde’s release clause currently standing at €60 million, Barcelona would be entitled to €12 million if PSG triggered it in January. What is interesting is that, initially Barcelona had retained 50% of Abde’s rights when they sold him to Betis in the summer of 2023. Barcelona could benefit from Abde’s move to PSG (Photo by Angel Martinez/Getty Images) However, that arrangement changed in the winter window of 2025, when Los Verdiblancos acquired an additional 30% in exchange for terminating Vitor Roque’s loan agreement, allowing Barça to sell him to Palmeiras. Nonetheless, they still hold a significant financial interest in Abde’s future. A transfer at the full release-clause value would deliver a useful injection of revenue at a time when the club are looking for defensive reinforcements. However, as per the report, Real Betis are not believed to be particularly keen on selling the winger, which could complicate any approach from PSG. For now, Barcelona will be watching developments closely, knowing that a deal could bring them €12 million from a player who left the club three years ago.

top.description: Brothers Brody and Danny Kenney started playing football together four years ago. “Brody convinced me to play,” said Danny, who was born a minute before Brody. On Wednesday, the 17-year-old twins from Leominster will suit up as seniors for St. Bernard’s in their final high school football game together during a Thanksgiving Eve tussle against Oakmont. “Playing with a twin has been nothing but the best,” said Danny, a wide receiver and safety who plays basketball in the winter. “I know I always have someone on my side looking out for me.” “It means a lot to (share) the field with Danny for our last Thanksgiving game,” said Brody, a tight end and linebacker who plays ice hockey in the winter. “I couldn’t be more thankful for having him by my side.” A day later, brothers Dean and Max Furcillo will share the football field for one last time during Nashoba’s Thanksgiving Day clash with Clinton. “It’s honestly special and rare,” said Max, a senior tight end who started playing football four years ago along with his younger sibling. “I’m going to look back on this forever.” “I want to end with a win for him,” said Dean, a sophomore quarterback. With a bunch of brother tandems (including a handful of twins) linking up on the gridiron this fall, the terrific trio of turkey, touchdowns and twinning is what’s on the menu for high school football teams across Central Mass. this Thanksgiving. So, the T&G caught up with a collection of varsity siblings to talk pigskin and turkey ahead of their holiday games. Bon appétit. Twinning Brothers Anthony and Tyrell Williams were excited to share the spotlight this season as a pair of senior running backs with the St. Bernard’s football team. But during the Bernardians’ first scrimmage on Sept. 1, Tyrell suffered a spinal compression fracture. “I honestly didn’t know if that (injury) was going to be the end of my season,” said Tyrell, who is 17 and was born three minutes after this twin brother. Luckily, Tyrell rejoined the Bernardians in time for their win over Oxford on Oct. 30. A week later, Anthony scored four rushing touchdowns while Tyrell caught a TD pass in a playoff victory over Easthampton. Tyrell then scored the game-tying touchdown with 31 seconds left to help St. Bernard’s beat Blue Hills, 21-20, on Nov. 13 to secure a spot in the Division 7 state semifinals. “I’m just grateful it healed over time and I’m back,” Tyrell told the T&G last week. “I was pumped up that I could play with my brother again.” “It's a blessing,” Anthony said. “I’m grateful.” Beyond the St. Bernard’s Kenney and Williams brothers, there are a trio of other twin tandems that teamed up in Central Mass. this fall. top.title: Todd McLellan excited about adding Kirby Dach to Red Wings lineup
top.description: The Detroit Red Wings anticipate newcomer Kirby Dach being in the lineup for their next game. That comes against the Vancouver Canucks at Little Caesars Arena on Wednesday, Nov. 25 (7:30 p.m., Detroit SportsNet), giving Dach one practice and one morning skate to adjust to his new teammates. Dach was part of the haul the Wings acquired from the Montreal Canadiens on Sunday in the Dylan Larkin trade, the centerpiece of which was 20-year-old center Michael Hage, who plays for Michigan. While Hage is the future, Dach is the present. The 6-foot-4, 221-pound 25-year-old has posted 144 points in 328 career NHL games since being drafted No. 3 overall in 2019 by the Chicago Blackhawks . OFF THE HORCOFF: Wings interim GM on why he finally traded Dylan Larkin "I'm excited about getting him here," coach Todd McLellan said after Monday's practice. "He's a young man that was drafted really high and probably rushed into the league. We all do that with those kids, probably a little too quick and probably affected his confidence. But I've been watching him lately, and it looks like he's playing some of his better hockey." Dach was en route to Detroit on Monday afternoon, after getting his work visa in order. So was goaltender Sam Montembeault, also part of the trade, but he has been injured. How much Dach can help the Wings (who are 8-12-3 after losing eight of their past 10 games) remains to be seen, but at least he gives them some added depth down the middle. "I think he has a physical side of the game that he can add to our locker room and hopefully that could be beneficial," Moritz Seider said. "I think maybe he's excited for a little bit of a change-up. He can be a big player, tall, obviously a lot of skill, plays on the wing, on the center. So I think we're all excited for him to come here." As for finally being done with the Larkin saga – at least until he and his Canadiens visit LCA on Feb. 18 – players in the Wings locker room sounded relieved it was over. "As much as we've tried to compartmentalize and separate it, and I think we've done a pretty good job of that," Andrew Copp said, "you leave the rink and it's everywhere. It's as soon as you go to your phone, you got friends asking about it, that kind of thing. So I think we've done a really good job as a team, but it'll be nice to just move on from the whole situation." News of the trade broke Sunday evening, a little before 9 p.m. "I was sitting on my couch, and texts started flowing in pretty quickly," Copp said. "It's been out there for a long time, the trade request, that it's almost like there isn't a reaction. He's been separated from the team for a few weeks now, so that part has already happened. Publicly, it's already happened, he hasn't been in the room. We're adding a player, or two players to our team, and it's just kind of going from there." top.title: Nassim Dahman named kicker eFootballer of the Year 2026
top.description: Nassim Dahman named kicker eFootballer of the Year 2026 The award is staying in Leipzig! Nassim “Nassada” Dahman has been named eFootballer of the Year 2026 . The kicker editorial team voted the RBLZ new signing Germany’s best eFootballer of the year following his first nomination. He beat a field of nominees that also included two of his current teammates, Levy Finn Rieck and Alihan Hadzhi . It’s the sixth time that the award has gone to an RBLZ Gaming player. Dahman becomes the third RBLZ player to win it, following in the footsteps of Umut Gültekin (2020 to 2023) and Levy Finn Rieck (2025). A memorable year capped by a fourth-place finish in Paris Nassada laid the foundations for his success early in the season. He secured his place at the World Championship back in January by reaching the quarter-finals of the FC Pro Open in London. It was the first time that his club at the time, SC Freiburg, had qualified for the World Championship. Nassada was then crowned German champion in April . He came out on top against the best players in the Virtual Bundesliga at the individual championship, beating RBLZ player Alihan Hadzhi in a thrilling final. Dahman proved that he was among the world’s best at the FC Pro World Championship in July. He finished second in the league phase with 15 points from six games to qualify directly for the round of 16, where he recorded a 9-1 win. He then beat world number one and former RBLZ player Anders Vejrgang 11-5 in the quarter-finals. Defeats in the semi-finals and the third-place play-off meant he ultimately finished fourth out of the 36 best players in the world. Making an instant impact in Leipzig Nassada has wasted little time settling in at RBLZ Gaming. He and Alihan Hadzhi played a key role in the team’s victory at the first VBL Club Championship Offline Showdown at the Allianz Arena in Munich. In the round of 16 against Holstein Kiel, he came from 3-1 down to win his singles match 4-3 with a last-minute goal. In the final against SC Paderborn 07, his 8-6 win over Jonas “Jonny” Wirth in extra time secured a 12-11 aggregate victory. Nassim Dahman: “It’s a huge honour to be named kicker eFootballer of the Year 2026. Having won the VBL title, I’m incredibly proud to round off the season with this award. Joining RBLZ Gaming was an important next step for me as I look to build on my success and win international titles with the team.” Nassada will be presented with the trophy on 14th November during the second VBL Club Championship Showdown at XPERION Berlin. top.title: Michigan basketball ready for return of Las Vegas vibes
top.description: For the first time since Jan. 27, 2025, Michigan men's basketball is not ranked. The Wolverines fell out of the USA TODAY Sports Men's Basketball Coaches Poll on Monday, Nov. 23, after their 79-73 loss to Villanova in Philadelphia on Saturday. The defeat was rough for the Wolverines, who shot 39.7% from the floor, 22.6% on 3s, turned the ball over more than twice as much as Villanova (16-7) and got just nine points from their reserves. The Wolverines spent the night in Philly recovering before flying directly to Las Vegas on Sunday, as they prepare for the Players Era 16 tournament. That begins with their fourth Big East opponent in six games this season, Creighton (4-1), on Tuesday (5:30 p.m., ESPN). FINDING ITS FOOTING: Michigan basketball finding its identity, forged by foe's speed U-M is 1-2 already against the Big East, with losses to UConn and Villanova sandwiched around a win over Marquette. There is recent history to suggest U-M should be able to bounce back. Michigan is 5-0 in midseason tournaments over the past two seasons, going 2-0 in the Fort Myers Tip-Off in November 2024 and sweeping November 2025's Players Era Championship in historic fashion – three wins in three days by 100 points combined. Moreover, Michigan is 18-2 in all neutral-site tournaments – including, of course, 6-0 in this spring's 2026 NCAA Tournament – over the past two seasons. “It's been a pretty big part of what we believe has helped our teams become more connected,” coach Mike Boynton Jr. recently told reporters. “People do believe that translates into on-court success. There's no real science behind that, I don't think. But I do think that the teams that we've had the last few years have become closer on these road trips because we have spent that time together. "I do think there's an element of them trusting each other, feeling confident that they have each other's best interest on the court that's helping in games.” For many of this season's Wolverines, it's a new experience. Columbia transfer Kenny Noland, who called it "high level" hoops, said he remembers taking notice of the way U-M was "smacking" opponents in Las Vegas last year, even while he was in the Ivy League. For freshmen such as Quinn Costello, it's the first college tournament, a test on quick turnarounds and new environments. Even though he was smiling after the Bulldogs' win, he also looked tired. “I played a lot of football today man,” Paulino said. “But you know what, it’s fun, when you get to this level you want to be playing as much as you can. top.title: Mauricio Pochettino identifies January priority as Man Utd prepare move for Benjamin Sesko alternative
top.description: Liverpool v Manchester United - Premier League 2026/27 - Getty Images Sport Despite possessing the most porous defence across Europe's top five leagues after a heavy defeat at Liverpool, Mauricio Pochettino will prioritise signing a striker in January. Manchester United's summer gamble in attack has backfired due to injury, prompting the club to seek a reliable alternative ahead of the winter window. Pochettino ignores defence to prioritise January striker Pochettino will focus on recruiting a new forward rather than strengthening United's leaky defence in the January transfer window. Sunday's 4-0 defeat at Liverpool left United with the most porous backline in any of Europe's top five leagues. Michael Carrick's successor received an immediate reality check at Anfield, with United entrenched in the relegation zone after 11 matches. Despite those glaring defensive flaws, Pochettino views the opposite end of the pitch as an equal concern. The Red Devils opted against signing a forward during the summer window, a decision that has spectacularly backfired. The club's hierarchy now has just over a month to identify attacking reinforcements before trading resumes. Injury crisis forces search for reliable forward United's attacking woes stem from a nagging shin injury suffered by Benjamin Sesko . The 23-year-old Slovenia international showed promise after a difficult start following his £74 million move from RB Leipzig last season, yet he has managed just six appearances this term. With Sesko unlikely to return until the New Year at the earliest, Pochettino has alternated between Bryan Mbuemo and Matheus Cunha in central striking roles. Joshua Zirkzee remains largely untrusted to lead the line. According to The Times , Pochettino will seek a "more reliable option" to cover for Zirkzee as soon as the January window opens. Securing a dependable focal point is now paramount to lifting United out of danger. Anfield humiliation exposes United's severe defensive frailties Pochettino's decision to prioritise a striker comes despite a harrowing defensive display against Andoni Iraola's Liverpool side. The Argentine handed Matthijs de Ligt a surprise start, but the Netherlands international struggled against a lively attack while still returning from a long-term injury. Matters worsened when Leny Yoro was sent off after just eight minutes at Anfield. Senior defenders Lisandro Martinez, Harry Maguire and Diogo Dalot also failed to impress under relentless pressure. Even with his rearguard leaking goals at an alarming rate, Pochettino believes adding firepower is the most pressing task for his struggling squad. GAME OF THE WEEK Lubbock-Cooper Liberty (12-0) vs. Brock (11-1) 2 p.m. Friday, Wildcat Stadium, Abilene This one has been expected for quite some time. As Lubbock-Cooper Liberty and Brock rolled through dominant regular seasons, this Thanksgiving-week matchup looked more and more likely. Now one of Class 4A Division II's contenders will bow out. The No. 3 Patriots remain unscathed, although last week's area playoff was tighter than projected. Monahans played tough before a 28-14 Liberty win. The game was tied at 7 at halftime. Patriots junior Kaiden Joseph ran for 225 yards and three touchdowns as he continued a torrid playoff pace. He notched 234 yards and four TDs in the first round against Burkburnett. Brock boasts an impressive resume itself. The second-ranked Eagles' lone loss is 38-27 at Anna, an undefeated 5A D-II squad prepping for its own regional semifinal. Among Brock's most impressive results is a 59-7 win over district foe Graham, which plays in the other Region I-4A D-II semifinal Friday. The Eagles enter off a 68-6 win over Big Spring. That continued a stretch of six consecutive games Brock has allowed seven points or fewer. The Eagles average 10.2 points allowed on the season. top.title: $250 scholarship to help Bloomington student try basketball
top.description: A $250 scholarship is helping a Fairview Elementary School fourth grader get a chance to try basketball through Bloomington Parks and Recreation. Ma'Siah Hanson received the fall Don Shiflet Memorial Scholarship, according to a community announcement. Hanson plans to use the award to play Bloomington Youth Basketball at Twin Lakes Recreation Center in January. Hanson is a longtime participant in the Banneker Afterschool program and a member of the Fairview Chess Club. His athletic interests include gymnastics, martial arts and football, and he is eager to try basketball. The Don Shiflet Memorial Scholarship provides two awards annually to Fairview Elementary students in the Banneker Afterschool program. Each $250 scholarship can help pay registration fees, equipment, uniforms and other gear needed to participate in a program through Bloomington Parks and Recreation or another local youth sports organization. Scholarship honors Don Shiflet's work with young athletes Shiflet's family established the scholarship after his death in 2019 to honor his commitment to helping young athletes and making sports more accessible to children in the community. Shiflet played a role in starting youth football and baseball programs in Bloomington and surrounding communities. He was inducted into the Monroe County Sports Hall of Fame in 2011 and was a charter member of the Bloomington Softball Hall of Fame. His involvement with the local softball community stretched back decades. Shiflet helped build Parks and Recreation's adult softball program beginning in 1952. The Lower Cascades North ball diamond was named Don Shiflet Field in 2001 in recognition of that service. He also spent 53 years working in sporting goods sales, providing athletic equipment to Indiana University and dozens of schools across Indiana. According to the announcement, family members said that Shiflet quietly helped young athletes whose families couldn't afford the equipment or clothing they needed to participate. "Don was known for never turning away someone in need, whether it be new shoes or a new glove or a pair of athletic shorts. His generosity was never forgotten by those he helped throughout the years," Kelsey Pearson, Fairview Elementary School assistant principal and Shiflet's granddaughter, said in the announcement. "One of Dad’s greatest joys was helping kids," Shiflet's daughter, Tammy Brannon, said in the announcement. "He was always willing to help kids out, especially those who might not otherwise have the opportunity to participate." Brannon said that her father had a special place in his heart for children involved in programming at Banneker Community Center. His family wanted the scholarship to reflect his kindness, generosity and love of youth sports. "Our family could not think of a better way to carry on his legacy than through setting up a scholarship to benefit local youth wanting to play sports," Pearson said in the announcement. Photos spanning the 1940s through 2025 offer a visual journey through more than eight decades of the rivalry, capturing how one of South Carolina’s biggest sports traditions changed while its intensity endured. Among the earliest images is an aerial view of the parking lot at the 1949 game, a scene frozen in time more than 75 years ago. Other photos connect the rivalry to history beyond football. The 1963 game, originally scheduled for Nov. 23, was postponed after the assassination of President John F. Kennedy and played on Thanksgiving Day. Clemson won 24-20. U.S. Sen. Strom Thurmond attended the 1965 game. The gallery also traces the coaches and players who defined different eras. Clemson’s Frank Howard and South Carolina’s Paul Dietzel appear in earlier years, followed by Clemson’s Danny Ford and South Carolina’s Joe Morrison. Later matchups featured Clemson’s Tommy Bowden against Lou Holtz and Dabo Swinney against Steve Spurrier. More recent images include Clemson quarterbacks Deshaun Watson, Trevor Lawrence, and Cade Klubnik, as well as South Carolina coaches Will Muschamp and Shane Beamer. But the famous faces are only part of the story. Packed stands, spirited tailgaters and fans dressed in orange or garnet reveal how generations made this rivalry their own. top.title: Isack Hadjar frustrated – What really happened on Red Bull's team radio in Las Vegas
top.description: Motorsport photo Isack Hadjar started Formula 1’s Las Vegas Grand Prix from fourth on the grid, and by lap four he had already found himself running second, right behind Red Bull team-mate Max Verstappen . And given that the grand prix had turned into what can only be described as a slipstreaming battle of the kind normally associated with track cycling, it was almost inevitable that Hadjar would sooner or later have a go at taking the lead. But a reminder from his race engineer Richard Wood was not long in coming. The priority, Wood explained, was to avoid losing time as a team. Red Bull needed to build a gap to George Russell , rather than waste precious seconds fighting among themselves. And Hadjar, certainly no stranger to self-confidence but ultimately a loyal Red Bull team player, complied. Eventually, he found himself alongside Verstappen again on the long straight towards Turn 14. But the Dutchman had no intention of surrendering the lead without a fight. "Can he stop defending? Otherwise I just gotta lose time," Hadjar complained over the radio. Wood, however, stuck to the plan they had already agreed upon: "Team request is to defend against George, otherwise we will be yo-yoing." At that point, Russell was the closest pursuer of the Red Bull Express at the front, with the trio merrily swapping positions. On one occasion, Russell even managed to overtake both Red Bulls simultaneously, only to find himself back in third place two or three corners later. In Las Vegas, slipstreaming and energy management were powerful weapons. More powerful, in fact, than outright speed. Hadjar's radio messages made it clear that, from a team perspective, he would have preferred something resembling a rotating paceline in cycling over conventional formation driving: a group of riders works together by constantly rotating the lead, allowing each member to benefit from the slipstream and enabling the group as a whole to travel faster than an individual rider could manage alone. But Red Bull, apparently caught somewhat off guard by the peculiar dynamics of the race, did not seem particularly interested in Hadjar's proposal. The idea of sharing the lead in order to open up a gap to Russell was not even discussed with Verstappen. At least, there is no corresponding question to be heard on the Dutchman's official onboard radio feed. nigeria.title: Questions Linger After Jensen Huang’s Return To Nvidia
nigeria.description: Jensen Huang’s surprise return to Nvidia on Monday appeared to stabilize the US chip giant, along with the broader stock market and AI ecosystem, but questions linger about the longterm impact of his scandal. Is Nvidia in the clear? An internal investigation overseen by independent directors is still underway at Nvidia regarding concerns that Huang might have been the target of an espionage campaign by China. US government officials, including President Donald Trump, assured Nvidia’s board that reinstating the company’s cofounder “poses no national security risk.” Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang (R) speaks alongside US President Donald Trump about investing in America, at the White House in Washington, DC, on April 30, 2025. Photo by JIM WATSON / AFP In parallel, the US Department of Justice is investigating Megaspeed, a company based in Singapore that allegedly bought processors from Nvidia and routed them to Chinese customers, circumventing US export restrictions. The Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) has also reportedly launched an investigation into Nvidia’s accounting practices and potentially misleading communication to shareholders. However, the Trump administration has generally avoided going after its allies, so the federal probes might not result in much, Columbia University Professor Eric Talley said. Will Huang be held accountable? Nvidia founder and CEO Jensen Huang speaks during Nvidia Live at CES 2026 ahead of the annual Consumer Electronics Show in Las Vegas, Nevada, on January 5, 2026. The embattled chief will nevertheless have to explain himself to lawmakers at a closed-door hearing on December 1 before three House committees. He will also testify before a Senate committee on December 3 in a hearing that will be livestreamed, while California’s attorney general has opened an investigation into the company’s chip exports and shareholder disclosures. There are plenty of regulators who are willing to push back against the Trump administration and ask tough questions, Talley said. Trump is also known to flip on people whom he no longer considers friends. “He can become estranged with people, and if that would happen with Jensen Huang, I can imagine a boomerang” on the Trump administration’s approach, Talley said. What does the board’s future look like? The logo of Nvidia is seen during a production preview exhibition in Taipei on May 21, 2025. Photo by I-HWA CHENG / AFP Openly opposed to Huang’s return before ultimately reinstating him, the board is in a delicate position. Former Goldman Sachs chief Lloyd Blankfein predicts its days may be numbered. A revolt by shareholders, many of whom supported the reinstatement of the 63-year-old entrepreneur, could reshape the board as soon as 2027, since all directors stand for reappointment every year. If they are spared, the directors could keep Huang on a much “shorter leash” compared to its history of largely deferring to the overwhelming power of this extraordinary executive, Talley said.

nigeria.title: Canada PM brings Trump impersonator on stage during press gala
nigeria.description: Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney invited a Donald Trump impersonator on stage during a weekend press gala, a move one critic said risks provoking a president known to bristle at being mocked. Carney was making a lighthearted speech at the Canadian equivalent of the White House Correspondents’ Dinner when he announced he was pressing an “emergency comedy button.” Comedian Mark McKinney, who impersonates Carney, came out first, followed by Trump impersonator Mark Critch, who appears on the long-running Canadian sketch comedy show “This Hour Has 22 Minutes.” “We’ve got two Carneys here, it’s a disaster,” Critch joked as Trump, before taking shots at Washington’s controversial ambassador to Canada and the White House press secretary vacancy, after Katie Zacharia left the role in just five days. With the United States and Canada still locked in a trade war, Critch offered some comic assurances about an impending pact. “Mark, we’re gonna have an incredible deal,” he said, mimicking Trump. “There’s only one thing standing in the way — me, because I’m crazy.” The bit appeared to go down well with reporters in Ottawa, but one of Carney’s political rivals was unimpressed. “I think provoking President Trump is arrogant, stupid and not funny,” said Yves-Francois Blanchet, the leader of the separatist Bloc Quebecois. He noted that Trump’s tariffs, including those affecting an aluminum industry central to Quebec’s economy, are causing real economic pain. “Quebec is paying the highest price for these tariffs…which should not be inflamed with bad jokes,” Blanchet said. Trump and Carney have both offered optimism that trade talks are progressing, but there were similarly positive comments in the days before negotiations collapsed in August. Canada wants relief from tariffs on key sectors, notably autos, but Ottawa has warned that completely removing the levies is unlikely and the Canadian economy needs to adjust to a permanently altered trading relationship with the United States. nigeria.title: Six killed, several injured in Delta political campaign clash – Police
nigeria.description: The Nigeria Police Force has confirmed that six people died and several others sustained injuries during a violent incident at a political campaign event in Uduere community, Ughelli North Local Government Area of Delta State. The Force also said the Inspector-General of Police, Olatunji Disu, had ordered a comprehensive investigation into the incident, including the actions of police officers deployed to the venue. CSP Ani Iniedu, the Force Public Relations Officer, disclosed this in a statement on Tuesday, adding that preliminary police findings indicated that six people were killed. “Preliminary Police reports indicate that six persons lost their lives, while several others sustained injuries. “The Force is aware of varying casualty figures circulating in the public domain. An ongoing investigation will establish the verified number of casualties and determine the circumstances surrounding the incident,” the statement read. Iniedu said the IGP had instructed the Delta State Commissioner of Police to conduct a thorough, impartial and evidence-based investigation. He added that the probe would examine the sequence of events, establish the identities of those involved and determine the circumstances surrounding the shooting, including the actions and deployment of police personnel at the scene. The Force also confirmed that the Delta State Government had imposed a dusk-to-dawn curfew across Ughelli North Local Government Area, running from 6pm to 6am daily until further notice. “In response to the security situation, the Delta State Government has imposed a dusk-to-dawn curfew across Ughelli North Local Government Area, from 6:00 p.m. to 6:00 a.m. daily, until further notice. The Delta State Police Command is enforcing the directive and has intensified security measures to prevent further breakdown of law and order,” the statement read. The police urged residents, community leaders, political stakeholders and campaign groups to remain peaceful, obey the curfew and refrain from circulating unverified reports that could worsen tensions. It also called on anyone with useful information, photographs, video footage or other evidence to assist the investigation by submitting them through established police channels, assuring that the identity of informants would be protected. The police confirmation followed an earlier allegation by the campaign organisation of former Deputy President of the Senate, Ovie Omo-Agege, that gunmen attacked his entourage during a campaign tour of the area. For years I lived with the pain and the burden of carrying this tumour on my face. Today, I feel hopeful again,” he said. ‎The teenager had earlier told Daily Trust that the illness had forced him out of school and shattered his dreams, as his family could not afford the cost of treatment. ‎In a further boost to his recovery and future, the foundation also pledged to support his long-term rehabilitation by either sponsoring his education or providing him with full startup capital to establish a business and become self-reliant. ‎‎A representative of the foundation said the decision was informed by the need to ensure that the teenager not only receives medical care but also has the opportunity to build a productive life after recovery. ‎‎“Our concern is not limited to the surgery alone. We want him to be able to stand on his own feet and pursue his dreams. Whether through formal education or entrepreneurship, we will support him to become self-reliant,” the representative said.

business.title: Strive (ASST) Buys No Bitcoin Last Week, Holdings Stay at 43,404 BTC
business.description: Bitcoin Magazine Strive (ASST) Buys No Bitcoin Last Week, Holdings Stay at 43,404 BTC Strive (Nasdaq: ASST) bought no bitcoin last week and sold no stock to fund new purchases, leaving its holdings unchanged at 43,404 BTC, according to a Monday 8-K filing. The Dallas-based company reported that its bitcoin count was unchanged between Nov. 13 and Nov. 20. It sold no Class A common shares, no SATA preferred shares and no SATS preferred shares in its at-the-market programs from the Nov. 13 close through the Nov. 20 close. Strive pauses after two small buys The pause follows a slowdown from the October sprint that built the stack. Strive bought 251 bitcoin for $17.5 million the prior week at an average of $69,853 per coin, after adding just 29 coins the week before that. Bitcoin traded near $61,000 on Coinbase on Monday afternoon. That is about 12.6% below the $69,853 average Strive paid for its most recent purchase. At that price, the 43,404-coin stack is worth roughly $2.65 billion. The filing gives no reason for the pause, and the company has not said whether it plans to resume weekly buying. Strive has typically disclosed its holdings on Mondays, so next week’s update will show whether the stack grows again. Most of the stack was built quickly. Strive held 28,000 bitcoin on Sept. 30 and acquired 15,124 more between Oct. 1 and Oct. 30, including a single 6,182-coin purchase. The company closed a registered offering of 7 million SATS shares on Oct. 20 for about $609 million in net proceeds, which funded much of that run. Cash and preferred holdings Strive’s cash and cash equivalents slipped to $462.4 million as of Nov. 20 from $465.3 million a week earlier, a decline of $2.9 million. The filing does not break out what drove the change. The company also still holds 505,000 shares of Strategy’s variable-rate STRC preferred stock. The fair value of that position fell to $47.3 million from $50.5 million, a drop of about $3.2 million, with the share count unchanged. Share counts were also flat. Strive reported 118,133,002 Class A shares and 9,198,107 Class B shares, for 127,331,109 effective common shares. Outstanding preferred stood at 14,030,176 shares of SATA and 7,141,037 shares of SATS, the 15% perpetual preferred it has used to fund most of its purchases. Strive’s holdings rose from 43,153 bitcoin on Nov. 6 to 43,404 on Nov. 13, and the filing shows no change since. With no common or preferred stock sold, the company raised no new capital through its offering programs last week, which left cash as its main resource for dividends and operations. The stock opened near $17.64, a gain of more than 20%, and gave back much of it through the session. business.title: Bitcoin Price Fades Near $61,000 as Stocks Soar on Huang’s Return
business.description: Bitcoin Magazine Bitcoin Price Fades Near $61,000 as Stocks Soar on Huang’s Return The bitcoin price slipped back to near $61,100 on Monday afternoon, giving up nearly all of its morning spike even as Wall Street held one of its biggest rallies in years on Nvidia’s decision to reinstate Jensen Huang as CEO. Bitcoin jumped above $64,000 shortly after the Nvidia news broke before 10 a.m. ET and topped out near $64,500. The move reversed within hours , and the bitcoin price dipped to around $60,800 by 2:45 p.m. ET. It remains up only modestly on the day. The round trip was costly for leveraged traders. Bitcoin liquidations reached about $321 million , with short bets making up $224 million of that total. Liquidations across the broader crypto market topped $762 million. Stocks hold gains as bitcoin fades Stocks kept climbing while bitcoin slid. The Nasdaq Composite was up about 6.9% near 24,170 at about 3:40 p.m. ET, while the S&P 500 gained about 5% and the Dow rose about 3.2%. The S&P 500 had fallen seven straight days before Monday. Nvidia (NVDA) led the move, trading near $165.66, up about 32% from Friday’s close of $125.53. The board voted unanimously to bring Huang back as president, CEO and director, 12 days after he resigned. A stronger dollar may be weighing on the bitcoin price. The dollar index rose about 0.65% to 104.40 , its strongest level since April 2025, as the stock rebound put more Federal Reserve rate hikes back in play. The Fed meets Dec. 8-9, and a quarter-point hike remains the base case. Adam Haeems, head of asset management at Tesseract Group, pointed to steady selling during U.S. market hours since Huang first stepped down. “Bitcoin has fallen in seven of the eight U.S. sessions since Huang went, today’s included, and last week each session’s fall lined up with that day’s ETF outflow,” he said. Crypto stocks keep most of their gains Crypto stocks held up far better than the bitcoin price. Strategy (MSTR) was up about 9.3% near $85.03 in afternoon trading, after it disclosed a purchase of 457 bitcoin last week. Coinbase (COIN) gained about 6.7% to near $108.78, Robinhood (HOOD) rose about 8.8% to near $67.64 and Circle (CRCL) added about 8% to near $51.33. Miners with AI data center businesses posted the biggest moves. IREN (IREN) jumped about 23% to near $14.57, CleanSpark (CLSK) rose about 12.6% and MARA Holdings (MARA) gained about 10%. Core Scientific (CORZ) climbed about 9.4% and Riot Platforms (RIOT) added about 7.1%. ETF flows and inflation data are next Monday’s spot bitcoin ETF flows are the next test. The funds lost about $1.79 billion last week, their fourth straight week of net outflows, as bitcoin slid toward $58,000 on Friday and hit a weekend low near $55,100. “Tonight’s ETF flow figure is the first real test of this bounce,” Haeems said. entertainment.description: For many people, buying property is one of the biggest financial decisions they will ever make. Yet, knowing who to trust, how to verify ownership and whether a property is worth the investment can make the process overwhelming. It is a challenge Solape Fayemi hopes to address with the launch of Saina Properties , a real estate company now operating across Nigeria, the United Kingdom, the United States and the United Arab Emirates. Officially unveiled at an event held on 17 November at the Marriott Hotel, Ikeja GRA, Lagos, Saina Properties is built around a simple idea: property ownership should be guided by sound advice, proper verification and professional support, not just the excitement of closing a deal. For Solape, whose experience in the investment industry shaped her understanding of money, risk and wealth creation, the decision to establish the company came from recognising the need for a more considered approach to real estate. “We are not building Saina Properties because the world needs another company selling properties. We are building Saina because we believe there is room for a different kind of real estate experience. That philosophy is reflected in the company’s three core areas of expertise: Advisory & Verification, Sales & Brokerage, and Developments . Rather than focusing solely on connecting buyers to properties, Saina brings together the guidance investors need to assess opportunities, the support required to navigate property transactions, and involvement in real estate development. entertainment.title: Elizabeth Agboola: Your Next Flight From Nigeria Could Be Two Holidays in One. Here’s How
entertainment.description: Have you ever spent six hours in an airport waiting for your connecting flight, watching the departure screens, browsing duty-free shops and wondering what the city outside looks like? Perhaps you were connecting through Istanbul, Doha, Dubai or Addis Ababa. You were technically in another country, but the closest you came to experiencing it was buying a souvenir at the airport. What if I told you that some airlines could help you turn that connection into an additional holiday, sometimes even providing accommodation? Having travelled to more than 70 countries, I have learnt that one of the smartest ways to travel is to pay attention to the journey, not just the destination. Many Nigerians book international tickets based on price, travel time and baggage allowance. These are important considerations, but there is another question worth asking: What else can this ticket give me? I am talking about stopovers, not the hurried two-hour connection where you are running between terminals, but an intentional break in your journey that allows you to experience another destination before continuing to the country you originally planned to visit. And with the right airline, itinerary and travel documents, that additional experience might cost less than you imagine. It does not, by itself, explain how that light is arranged, divided or controlled. Those implementation choices can have a major influence on contrast, black level performance, highlight control and the visibility of blooming in difficult scenes. From Presence To Performance That distinction matters because a category becomes more useful to consumers when it can be evaluated through clear performance principles rather than through a technology name alone. For Mini LED, three factors provide a practical starting point. The first is hardware local dimming. In a hardware based system, physical groups of LEDs can be brightened, dimmed or switched off independently across different areas of the screen. This gives the television more direct control over how light is distributed within a single image. The second is local dimming zone count and precision. A higher number of independently controlled zones can allow the backlight to respond in smaller areas, which can improve separation between bright highlights and surrounding dark regions when other major conditions are comparable. The number itself is not the whole story, but it is a useful indicator of how granular the backlight system can be. The third is backlight architecture. Full Array Local Dimming places controllable zones across the area behind the panel, providing the physical foundation for more localized light management than designs that illuminate the panel from the edges or operate the backlight more uniformly. Together, these three elements move the Mini LED conversation from a simple question of whether the technology is present to a more useful question: how effectively is the light being controlled? He was so convinced that I wondered whether a manual somewhere explained how men were manufactured. According to him, men were created to be strong, endure pain and keep their emotions to themselves. That was simply how they were made. “So, because you’re a man, you’re not supposed to feel hurt, fear or disappointment?” I disagreed. He insisted that showing emotions was not in a man’s nature. Who made that rule? Who decided that men could experience pain but must never be seen expressing it? At what point did being a man become synonymous with pretending that everything was fine? The conversation wilted, but it has stayed with me, perhaps because my friend wasn’t expressing an unusual opinion. He was repeating a stereotype many of us have heard all our lives: “Boys don’t cry.” “Be a man.” “Man up.” Three little expressions, and somewhere between being told to be strong and learning to say “I’m fine,” I wonder how many men have forgotten what it feels like to be heard. Frequent questions men are asked: “How far? Work nko?” “When are you getting married?” “Have you bought land?” “How is the family?” And the famous Nigerian question that can make an unemployed graduate dread family gatherings: “So, what are you doing now?” We often inquire about their achievements, responsibilities, and plans. These aspects are important, but how often do we ask about their fears? A father who leaves home before sunrise and returns exhausted, burdened by the weight of school fees, rent, and family expectations. A young graduate who has submitted countless job applications, yet still smiles politely when another relative inquires why he hasn’t found a job. A successful professional whose LinkedIn profile showcases numerous achievements, while his personal life tells a story that no one has thought to ask about. We admire their strength, we applaud their sacrifices, and we celebrate their accomplishments. But what about what they are going through? The person everyone leans on also needs somewhere to lean. sports.title: Barcelona in line for potential €12m windfall as former winger emerges as a target for PSG
sports.description: Barcelona in line for potential €12m windfall as former winger emerges as a target for PSG According to Le Parisien (h/t Mundo Deportivo ), PSG are considering a move for Real Betis winger Ez Abde as they prepare to strengthen their attack in January, and Barcelona could benefit financially from the operation. The 24-year-old former Blaugrana attacker is among the names being evaluated by PSG and a transfer could see the Catalans receive a potential €12 million windfall. PSG eyeing Abde The current French and European champions have been hurt by injuries in the attacking department as two regular starters, Khvicha Kvaratskhelia and Desire Doue, have both suffered from ruptured ACLs, ruling them out for a long period. Luis Enrique & co. still have the likes of Maghnes Akliouche and Mika Godts as alternatives, while two former Barcelona stars, Ferran Torres and Ousmane Dembele, are also optons even though they have played centrally in recent seasons. Nonetheless, PSG are looking at the market to reinforce their attacking unit and Abde, who has excelled at Real Betis since leaving Barcelona, has emerged as an option. PSG interested in Abde. (Photo by Octavio Passos/Getty Images) The Moroccan international is among several players that Les Parisiens are considering, including Antonio Nusa of RB Leipzig and Chelsea youngster Estevao, among others. Barcelona, though, will be watching the situation closely, as Abde’s transfer could bring them a sizeable revenue boost. Why Barcelona stand to gain That is because, the Blaugrana still retain a 20% stake in the winger’s economic rights when he joined Real Betis permanently. With Abde’s release clause currently standing at €60 million, Barcelona would be entitled to €12 million if PSG triggered it in January. What is interesting is that, initially Barcelona had retained 50% of Abde’s rights when they sold him to Betis in the summer of 2023. Barcelona could benefit from Abde’s move to PSG (Photo by Angel Martinez/Getty Images) However, that arrangement changed in the winter window of 2025, when Los Verdiblancos acquired an additional 30% in exchange for terminating Vitor Roque’s loan agreement, allowing Barça to sell him to Palmeiras. Nonetheless, they still hold a significant financial interest in Abde’s future. A transfer at the full release-clause value would deliver a useful injection of revenue at a time when the club are looking for defensive reinforcements. However, as per the report, Real Betis are not believed to be particularly keen on selling the winger, which could complicate any approach from PSG. For now, Barcelona will be watching developments closely, knowing that a deal could bring them €12 million from a player who left the club three years ago.

sports.title: Governor's Cup trivia: Can you pass our Louisville-Kentucky football quiz?
sports.description: Louisville football heads to Kentucky on Nov. 28 to compete in the annual Governor's Cup . Kentucky leads the Governor's Cup series 20-17, but last season, the Cardinals crushed the Wildcats 41-0 at L&N Stadium. It was one of the biggest blowouts in series history . Additionally, the Cardinals earned bragging rights for eliminating their rival from bowl eligibility. With the rich history between these two schools, you can test your knowledge here. How well do you know your Governor's Cup history? Question 1 : How many times have Louisville and Kentucky both been ranked entering the Governor's Cup? Question 2: Which current Louisville Bats baseball coach scored a touchdown in the 1998 Governor's Cup? Question 3: What was 2016 Heisman Trophy winner Lamar Jackson's career record vs. Kentucky? Question 4 : Kentucky quarterback Tim Couch was the No. 1 overall pick in the 1999 NFL Draft. What was his career record vs. Louisville? Question 5: Who is the only player to rush for 100 or more yards three times in Governor's Cup history? Question 6 : Who holds the single-game record for most rushing yards in the Governor's Cup? Question 7: Who were the first Kentucky and Louisville coaches to coach their teams in the Governor's Cup? Question 8: Who makes the Governor's Cup trophy? Question 9: How much does it cost to make the trophy? Question 10 : What was the longest Governor's Cup winning streak? Scroll for the answers Answer 1: Saturday's matchup at Kroger Field will be the first time that both enter as ranked teams — and only because both stayed in the US LBM Coaches Poll this week . Louisville moved up four spots to No. 18. Kentucky, which dropped out of the AP Top 25, held on to the No. 25 spot in the coaches poll. So the teams still have never met when both were in the AP Top 25. Answer 2: Kentucky receiver Vince Harrison, who caught a 23-yard pass from Tim Couch. Harrison, a two-sport standout at Kentucky, played two seasons for the football team before focusing on baseball. Tampa Bay selected Harrison in the 13th round of the 2001 MLB Draft. He advanced to Double-A before eventually retiring as a player in 2011. Answer 3: Jackson went 2-1 vs. Kentucky. The lone loss came during his 2016 Heisman season, even though he accounted for four touchdowns (two passing, two rushing) and 452 total yards (281 passing, 171 rushing). Answer 4: Couch also went 2-1 in the Governor's Cup. He set the series single-game record for passing yards (498) and touchdown passes (7) in Kentucky's 68-34 victory in 1998. Answer 5: Louisville legend Lamar Jackson, who rushed for 186 yards in 2015, 171 yards in 2016 and 156 yards in 2017. Answer 6: Kentucky's Lynn Bowden rushed for 284 yards in the Wildcats' 45-13 victory over Louisville in 2019. Bowden, if you recall, was a receiver who became the Wildcats' emergency quarterback following early-season injuries to UK's starter and backup. sports.title: These brother tandems team up one final time for Thanksgiving football
sports.description: Brothers Brody and Danny Kenney started playing football together four years ago. “Brody convinced me to play,” said Danny, who was born a minute before Brody. On Wednesday, the 17-year-old twins from Leominster will suit up as seniors for St. Bernard’s in their final high school football game together during a Thanksgiving Eve tussle against Oakmont. “Playing with a twin has been nothing but the best,” said Danny, a wide receiver and safety who plays basketball in the winter. “I know I always have someone on my side looking out for me.” “It means a lot to (share) the field with Danny for our last Thanksgiving game,” said Brody, a tight end and linebacker who plays ice hockey in the winter. “I couldn’t be more thankful for having him by my side.” A day later, brothers Dean and Max Furcillo will share the football field for one last time during Nashoba’s Thanksgiving Day clash with Clinton. “It’s honestly special and rare,” said Max, a senior tight end who started playing football four years ago along with his younger sibling. “I’m going to look back on this forever.” “I want to end with a win for him,” said Dean, a sophomore quarterback. With a bunch of brother tandems (including a handful of twins) linking up on the gridiron this fall, the terrific trio of turkey, touchdowns and twinning is what’s on the menu for high school football teams across Central Mass. this Thanksgiving. So, the T&G caught up with a collection of varsity siblings to talk pigskin and turkey ahead of their holiday games. Bon appétit. Twinning Brothers Anthony and Tyrell Williams were excited to share the spotlight this season as a pair of senior running backs with the St. Bernard’s football team. But during the Bernardians’ first scrimmage on Sept. 1, Tyrell suffered a spinal compression fracture. “I honestly didn’t know if that (injury) was going to be the end of my season,” said Tyrell, who is 17 and was born three minutes after this twin brother. Luckily, Tyrell rejoined the Bernardians in time for their win over Oxford on Oct. 30. A week later, Anthony scored four rushing touchdowns while Tyrell caught a TD pass in a playoff victory over Easthampton. Tyrell then scored the game-tying touchdown with 31 seconds left to help St. Bernard’s beat Blue Hills, 21-20, on Nov. 13 to secure a spot in the Division 7 state semifinals. “I’m just grateful it healed over time and I’m back,” Tyrell told the T&G last week. “I was pumped up that I could play with my brother again.” “It's a blessing,” Anthony said. “I’m grateful.” Beyond the St. Bernard’s Kenney and Williams brothers, there are a trio of other twin tandems that teamed up in Central Mass. this fall. sports.title: Todd McLellan excited about adding Kirby Dach to Red Wings lineup
sports.description: The Detroit Red Wings anticipate newcomer Kirby Dach being in the lineup for their next game. That comes against the Vancouver Canucks at Little Caesars Arena on Wednesday, Nov. 25 (7:30 p.m., Detroit SportsNet), giving Dach one practice and one morning skate to adjust to his new teammates. Dach was part of the haul the Wings acquired from the Montreal Canadiens on Sunday in the Dylan Larkin trade, the centerpiece of which was 20-year-old center Michael Hage, who plays for Michigan. While Hage is the future, Dach is the present. The 6-foot-4, 221-pound 25-year-old has posted 144 points in 328 career NHL games since being drafted No. 3 overall in 2019 by the Chicago Blackhawks . OFF THE HORCOFF: Wings interim GM on why he finally traded Dylan Larkin "I'm excited about getting him here," coach Todd McLellan said after Monday's practice. "He's a young man that was drafted really high and probably rushed into the league. We all do that with those kids, probably a little too quick and probably affected his confidence. But I've been watching him lately, and it looks like he's playing some of his better hockey." Dach was en route to Detroit on Monday afternoon, after getting his work visa in order. So was goaltender Sam Montembeault, also part of the trade, but he has been injured. How much Dach can help the Wings (who are 8-12-3 after losing eight of their past 10 games) remains to be seen, but at least he gives them some added depth down the middle. "I think he has a physical side of the game that he can add to our locker room and hopefully that could be beneficial," Moritz Seider said. "I think maybe he's excited for a little bit of a change-up. He can be a big player, tall, obviously a lot of skill, plays on the wing, on the center. So I think we're all excited for him to come here." As for finally being done with the Larkin saga – at least until he and his Canadiens visit LCA on Feb. 18 – players in the Wings locker room sounded relieved it was over. "As much as we've tried to compartmentalize and separate it, and I think we've done a pretty good job of that," Andrew Copp said, "you leave the rink and it's everywhere. It's as soon as you go to your phone, you got friends asking about it, that kind of thing. So I think we've done a really good job as a team, but it'll be nice to just move on from the whole situation." News of the trade broke Sunday evening, a little before 9 p.m. "I was sitting on my couch, and texts started flowing in pretty quickly," Copp said. "It's been out there for a long time, the trade request, that it's almost like there isn't a reaction. He's been separated from the team for a few weeks now, so that part has already happened. Publicly, it's already happened, he hasn't been in the room. We're adding a player, or two players to our team, and it's just kind of going from there." sports.title: Nassim Dahman named kicker eFootballer of the Year 2026
sports.description: Nassim Dahman named kicker eFootballer of the Year 2026 The award is staying in Leipzig! Nassim “Nassada” Dahman has been named eFootballer of the Year 2026 . The kicker editorial team voted the RBLZ new signing Germany’s best eFootballer of the year following his first nomination. He beat a field of nominees that also included two of his current teammates, Levy Finn Rieck and Alihan Hadzhi . It’s the sixth time that the award has gone to an RBLZ Gaming player. Dahman becomes the third RBLZ player to win it, following in the footsteps of Umut Gültekin (2020 to 2023) and Levy Finn Rieck (2025). A memorable year capped by a fourth-place finish in Paris Nassada laid the foundations for his success early in the season. He secured his place at the World Championship back in January by reaching the quarter-finals of the FC Pro Open in London. It was the first time that his club at the time, SC Freiburg, had qualified for the World Championship. Nassada was then crowned German champion in April . He came out on top against the best players in the Virtual Bundesliga at the individual championship, beating RBLZ player Alihan Hadzhi in a thrilling final. Dahman proved that he was among the world’s best at the FC Pro World Championship in July. He finished second in the league phase with 15 points from six games to qualify directly for the round of 16, where he recorded a 9-1 win. He then beat world number one and former RBLZ player Anders Vejrgang 11-5 in the quarter-finals. Defeats in the semi-finals and the third-place play-off meant he ultimately finished fourth out of the 36 best players in the world. Making an instant impact in Leipzig Nassada has wasted little time settling in at RBLZ Gaming. He and Alihan Hadzhi played a key role in the team’s victory at the first VBL Club Championship Offline Showdown at the Allianz Arena in Munich. In the round of 16 against Holstein Kiel, he came from 3-1 down to win his singles match 4-3 with a last-minute goal. In the final against SC Paderborn 07, his 8-6 win over Jonas “Jonny” Wirth in extra time secured a 12-11 aggregate victory. Nassim Dahman: “It’s a huge honour to be named kicker eFootballer of the Year 2026. Having won the VBL title, I’m incredibly proud to round off the season with this award. Joining RBLZ Gaming was an important next step for me as I look to build on my success and win international titles with the team.” Nassada will be presented with the trophy on 14th November during the second VBL Club Championship Showdown at XPERION Berlin. sports.title: Michigan basketball ready for return of Las Vegas vibes
sports.description: For the first time since Jan. 27, 2025, Michigan men's basketball is not ranked. The Wolverines fell out of the USA TODAY Sports Men's Basketball Coaches Poll on Monday, Nov. 23, after their 79-73 loss to Villanova in Philadelphia on Saturday. The defeat was rough for the Wolverines, who shot 39.7% from the floor, 22.6% on 3s, turned the ball over more than twice as much as Villanova (16-7) and got just nine points from their reserves. The Wolverines spent the night in Philly recovering before flying directly to Las Vegas on Sunday, as they prepare for the Players Era 16 tournament. That begins with their fourth Big East opponent in six games this season, Creighton (4-1), on Tuesday (5:30 p.m., ESPN). FINDING ITS FOOTING: Michigan basketball finding its identity, forged by foe's speed U-M is 1-2 already against the Big East, with losses to UConn and Villanova sandwiched around a win over Marquette. There is recent history to suggest U-M should be able to bounce back. Michigan is 5-0 in midseason tournaments over the past two seasons, going 2-0 in the Fort Myers Tip-Off in November 2024 and sweeping November 2025's Players Era Championship in historic fashion – three wins in three days by 100 points combined. Moreover, Michigan is 18-2 in all neutral-site tournaments – including, of course, 6-0 in this spring's 2026 NCAA Tournament – over the past two seasons. “It's been a pretty big part of what we believe has helped our teams become more connected,” coach Mike Boynton Jr. recently told reporters. “People do believe that translates into on-court success. There's no real science behind that, I don't think. But I do think that the teams that we've had the last few years have become closer on these road trips because we have spent that time together. "I do think there's an element of them trusting each other, feeling confident that they have each other's best interest on the court that's helping in games.” For many of this season's Wolverines, it's a new experience. For freshmen such as Quinn Costello, it's the first college tournament, a test on quick turnarounds and new environments. sports.title: Mauricio Pochettino identifies January priority as Man Utd prepare move for Benjamin Sesko alternative
sports.description: Liverpool v Manchester United - Premier League 2026/27 - Getty Images Sport Despite possessing the most porous defence across Europe's top five leagues after a heavy defeat at Liverpool, Mauricio Pochettino will prioritise signing a striker in January. Manchester United's summer gamble in attack has backfired due to injury, prompting the club to seek a reliable alternative ahead of the winter window. Pochettino ignores defence to prioritise January striker Pochettino will focus on recruiting a new forward rather than strengthening United's leaky defence in the January transfer window. Sunday's 4-0 defeat at Liverpool left United with the most porous backline in any of Europe's top five leagues. Michael Carrick's successor received an immediate reality check at Anfield, with United entrenched in the relegation zone after 11 matches. Despite those glaring defensive flaws, Pochettino views the opposite end of the pitch as an equal concern. The Red Devils opted against signing a forward during the summer window, a decision that has spectacularly backfired. The club's hierarchy now has just over a month to identify attacking reinforcements before trading resumes. Injury crisis forces search for reliable forward United's attacking woes stem from a nagging shin injury suffered by Benjamin Sesko . The 23-year-old Slovenia international showed promise after a difficult start following his £74 million move from RB Leipzig last season, yet he has managed just six appearances this term. With Sesko unlikely to return until the New Year at the earliest, Pochettino has alternated between Bryan Mbuemo and Matheus Cunha in central striking roles. Joshua Zirkzee remains largely untrusted to lead the line. According to The Times , Pochettino will seek a "more reliable option" to cover for Zirkzee as soon as the January window opens. Securing a dependable focal point is now paramount to lifting United out of danger. Anfield humiliation exposes United's severe defensive frailties Pochettino's decision to prioritise a striker comes despite a harrowing defensive display against Andoni Iraola's Liverpool side. The Argentine handed Matthijs de Ligt a surprise start, but the Netherlands international struggled against a lively attack while still returning from a long-term injury. Matters worsened when Leny Yoro was sent off after just eight minutes at Anfield. Senior defenders Lisandro Martinez, Harry Maguire and Diogo Dalot also failed to impress under relentless pressure. Even with his rearguard leaking goals at an alarming rate, Pochettino believes adding firepower is the most pressing task for his struggling squad. That hardly means, however, that the action around the league won’t be interesting as the regular season concludes. Here are our updated power rankings heading into Week 13. 1. Miami (Fla.) (10-1, 8-0) Last week: 1. This week: Boston College . What to know: With their spot in the title game secured, the Hurricanes hope to make short work of the Eagles for their home crowd. Standout WR Malachi Toney will likely be held out at least another week as he nears his return from an ankle procedure. 2. Wake Forest (10-1, 7-1) Last week: 2. This week: Duke. The Wildcats, however, will be just as motivated to snap their three-game skid after tasting the top 10. 4. Clemson (7-4, 5-3) Last week: 12. This week: South Carolina. What to know: To say the Tigers have been erratic is a bit of an understatement, losing to one of the ACC’s bottom teams one week and beating one of the best six days later. sports.title: $250 scholarship to help Bloomington student try basketball
sports.description: A $250 scholarship is helping a Fairview Elementary School fourth grader get a chance to try basketball through Bloomington Parks and Recreation. Ma'Siah Hanson received the fall Don Shiflet Memorial Scholarship, according to a community announcement. Hanson plans to use the award to play Bloomington Youth Basketball at Twin Lakes Recreation Center in January. Hanson is a longtime participant in the Banneker Afterschool program and a member of the Fairview Chess Club. His athletic interests include gymnastics, martial arts and football, and he is eager to try basketball. The Don Shiflet Memorial Scholarship provides two awards annually to Fairview Elementary students in the Banneker Afterschool program. Each $250 scholarship can help pay registration fees, equipment, uniforms and other gear needed to participate in a program through Bloomington Parks and Recreation or another local youth sports organization. Scholarship honors Don Shiflet's work with young athletes Shiflet's family established the scholarship after his death in 2019 to honor his commitment to helping young athletes and making sports more accessible to children in the community. Shiflet played a role in starting youth football and baseball programs in Bloomington and surrounding communities. He was inducted into the Monroe County Sports Hall of Fame in 2011 and was a charter member of the Bloomington Softball Hall of Fame. His involvement with the local softball community stretched back decades. Shiflet helped build Parks and Recreation's adult softball program beginning in 1952. The Lower Cascades North ball diamond was named Don Shiflet Field in 2001 in recognition of that service. He also spent 53 years working in sporting goods sales, providing athletic equipment to Indiana University and dozens of schools across Indiana. According to the announcement, family members said that Shiflet quietly helped young athletes whose families couldn't afford the equipment or clothing they needed to participate. "Don was known for never turning away someone in need, whether it be new shoes or a new glove or a pair of athletic shorts. His generosity was never forgotten by those he helped throughout the years," Kelsey Pearson, Fairview Elementary School assistant principal and Shiflet's granddaughter, said in the announcement. "One of Dad’s greatest joys was helping kids," Shiflet's daughter, Tammy Brannon, said in the announcement. Brannon said that her father had a special place in his heart for children involved in programming at Banneker Community Center. His family wanted the scholarship to reflect his kindness, generosity and love of youth sports. sports.title: Isack Hadjar frustrated – What really happened on Red Bull's team radio in Las Vegas
sports.description: Motorsport photo Isack Hadjar started Formula 1’s Las Vegas Grand Prix from fourth on the grid, and by lap four he had already found himself running second, right behind Red Bull team-mate Max Verstappen . And given that the grand prix had turned into what can only be described as a slipstreaming battle of the kind normally associated with track cycling, it was almost inevitable that Hadjar would sooner or later have a go at taking the lead. But a reminder from his race engineer Richard Wood was not long in coming. The priority, Wood explained, was to avoid losing time as a team. Red Bull needed to build a gap to George Russell , rather than waste precious seconds fighting among themselves. And Hadjar, certainly no stranger to self-confidence but ultimately a loyal Red Bull team player, complied. Eventually, he found himself alongside Verstappen again on the long straight towards Turn 14. But the Dutchman had no intention of surrendering the lead without a fight. "Can he stop defending? Otherwise I just gotta lose time," Hadjar complained over the radio. Wood, however, stuck to the plan they had already agreed upon: "Team request is to defend against George, otherwise we will be yo-yoing." At that point, Russell was the closest pursuer of the Red Bull Express at the front, with the trio merrily swapping positions. On one occasion, Russell even managed to overtake both Red Bulls simultaneously, only to find himself back in third place two or three corners later. In Las Vegas, slipstreaming and energy management were powerful weapons. More powerful, in fact, than outright speed. Hadjar's radio messages made it clear that, from a team perspective, he would have preferred something resembling a rotating paceline in cycling over conventional formation driving: a group of riders works together by constantly rotating the lead, allowing each member to benefit from the slipstream and enabling the group as a whole to travel faster than an individual rider could manage alone. But Red Bull, apparently caught somewhat off guard by the peculiar dynamics of the race, did not seem particularly interested in Hadjar's proposal. The idea of sharing the lead in order to open up a gap to Russell was not even discussed with Verstappen. At least, there is no corresponding question to be heard on the Dutchman's official onboard radio feed. technology.title: Education software supplier's legacy login system left 355,000 school email addresses exposed
technology.description: More than 355,000 school staff and pupil email addresses ended up in the hands of hackers who broke into UK education software supplier Bromcom in September. The breach was added to Have I Been Pwned on Monday, revealing that 355,051 unique email addresses were caught up in the incident. The data also included single sign-on (SSO) registration reference numbers, although Bromcom insists that no passwords or authentication tokens were stolen. As The Register reported in Octobe r , the attackers got in through a legacy SSO registration component in Bromcom's Communications Server environment. The technology had already been superseded but was still running because an internal system continued to use it. Bromcom discovered something was amiss on September 6 after customers reported problems accessing its SSO service. At the time, the company was still working with external forensic specialists to establish exactly what the intruders had managed to get their hands on. Bromcom's FAQ says its investigation is complete and confirms that the intruders used a script to extract SSO registration information from the compromised server. The supplier insists its Management Information System (MIS), used by schools to keep track of everything from attendance to pupil records, was untouched. The compromised service also couldn't be used to get into Microsoft or Google accounts, which have their own login systems. Bromcom has since pulled the plug on the old component, tightened its authorization checks, and added more security logging. It says it hasn't found any evidence of accounts being hijacked as a result of the breach. Bromcom also confirmed it hadn't reported the breach to the UK's Information Commission's Office. Its reasoning is that it was the data processor, not the controller, so any decision to involve the regulator was for the affected schools and academy trusts to make. As for the risk to staff and pupils, Bromcom considers it to be low. No passwords or pupil records held in the MIS were taken, it says, although schools have been advised to watch for phishing messages and suspicious requests to reset passwords or approve sign-ins. The supplier's software is used by more than 5,000 schools and 390 multi-academy trusts across the UK, though it hasn't said how many were caught up in this particular mess. The Register has asked Bromcom how many schools and pupils were affected, and whether the figure published by Have I Been Pwned matches its own findings, but has yet to receive a response. Bromcom kept the superseded component running because an internal system still needed it. Unfortunately, the intruders found a use for it too. ®

technology.title: Cisco and OpenAI pitch eBPF kernel plugins as the way to tame the patchpocalypse
technology.description: Cisco and OpenAI have released an open-source tool called Shirudo to implement compensating controls in Linux, potentially improving security for users who can’t quickly patch newly discovered software flaws. Shirudo relies on eBPF, the technology that makes it possible to run sandboxed programs in the Linux kernel. eBPF programs are effectively kernel plug-ins but don’t get unrestricted access to system resources. Developers have mostly used eBPF to create network functions that enable things like the open source Kubernetes observability and security tool Cilium , a Cloud Native Computing Foundation project. Cisco and OpenAI think eBPF can help organizations cope with the flood of 100,000-plus software flaws reported this year, many after the debut of AI-powered bug finders. The increased volume of flaws, and patches to fix them, is a problem for many organizations which already struggle to test fixes or find change windows in which to implement them. That problem has seen greater interest in “compensating controls” – changes to applications or infrastructure that harden them against flaws or malware, without requiring a patch. With Shirudo, Cisco and OpenAI are suggesting two things: The privileges eBPF programs enjoy make them a fine way to implement compensating controls for Linux; Agents should scan your infrastructure for vulnerabilities, then use tools like OpenAI’s Codex to write compensating controls as eBPF programs at machine speed. “Shirudo” is apparently the Japanese word for “shield,” so Cisco and OpenAI have called the eBPF programs the tool creates “shields.” The two companies envision humans checking every shield Shirudo creates before putting it into production. Shirudo is open source and available here . The two companies say they’ve already demonstrated it could mitigate the recently discovered flaws in Java without requiring downtime for an Elasticsearch implementation. Cisco and OpenAI are not alone in advocating for compensating controls. Third-party software maintenance outfits like Rimini Street have used them for years to protect software when their clients no longer have the right to access patches. VMware has introduced “virtual patching.” Palo Alto Networks and Rapid 7 also like this approach, and offer automation to develop controls. Where Cisco and OpenAI differ is their decision to make Shirudo open source , and their ambition that other players adapt and advance it. That offer is not entirely altruistic, as if Shirudo takes off it could create more demand for Codex. Cisco’s angle comes from the fact it owns Isovalent, an early champion of eBPF and the creator of both Cilium and the Tetragon sub-project on which Shirudo is based. Switchzilla is using eBPF in other products, so normalizing its use through an open source project can’t hurt. ®

But if the AI can’t explain what it’s “proven,” are we actually any closer to understanding anything, or have we simply built another black box? That question is top of mind among mathematicians and computer scientists this week after Anthropic researcher Levent Alpöge claimed to have solved a mathematical conjecture so elusive it's gone unproven for more than 150 years. The fact that this note came out one day after Anthropic's record-setting IPO is a coincidence, we're sure. In a four-page post to his website, the researcher described how with the help of Claude, he believes he has proven the Riemann Hypothesis, one of seven Millennium problems so complex and so important that the Clay Mathematics Institute has offered a $1 million prize to anyone who is successful in solving them. The Riemann Hypothesis, conjectured by German mathematician Bernhard Riemann in 1859, contends that all nontrivial zeros of the Riemann zeta function – those with a real part between zero and one – have a real part equal to 1/2. Confused? Don’t worry. We’ve linked to an explainer that goes into more detail here . What's important is that, if the Riemann Hypothesis is right, mathematicians can place tighter bounds on the difference between the actual distribution of prime numbers and mathematical estimates of that distribution. Researchers have previously attempted to disprove the conjecture through computational brute force, and therein have shown the hypothesis holds to at least 10 trillion zeros . There’s reason to believe that the Riemann Hypothesis is accurate, but the possibility remains that over a sufficiently long series the pattern might diverge. And so, more than 150 years after Riemann published his hypothesis, it has remained just that. Alpöge’s proof, if it can even be called that, is now the subject of great debate. The four pages in which Alpöge remarks on the discoveries he and Claude made aren’t exactly a proof, but rather 14 tarballs worth of Lean code totaling roughly 240 MB.
